claim: In the tested transgene system, tobacco etch virus P1/HC-Pro suppressed established posttranscriptional gene silencing, supporting the conclusion that a plant virus can counter an RNA-based host defense response.

experimental_context.genotype: silenced GUS transgene crossed with P1/HC-Pro transgene

limitations: The result is specific to the tested transgene/PTGS system and P1/HC-Pro.
It does not identify the complete host target set or establish that every viral suppressor uses the same mechanism.
This is a two-author team result, not evidence of a private or current personal view.

claim: HC-Pro inactivated pre-existing PTGS in the tested plant system while small RNAs were lost and DNA methylation was partially reduced, supporting a maintenance-stage effect rather than proving a single universal molecular target.

experimental_context.treatment: HC-Pro introduction by transient or transgenic expression

limitations: The paper supports a pathway-stage interpretation, not a complete physical target mechanism.
Species detail is kept at the authorized record boundary where the abstract is not explicit.

claim: Arabidopsis mutant analysis separated DCL1, DCL3 and DCL2 contributions to miRNA, endogenous siRNA and viral siRNA biogenesis, respectively, and linked RDR2 to the endogenous siRNAs tested.

entities.precursor: multiple endogenous and viral small-RNA precursors

experimental_context.tissue: Arabidopsis tissues used in mutant and infection assays
experimental_context.genotype: dcl1, dcl2, dcl3 and rdr2 insertion mutants
experimental_context.treatment: turnip crinkle virus infection for antiviral arm

limitations: Assignments are bounded to the alleles, loci and virus system tested.
Later work revealed redundancy and context dependence; the 2004 labels should not be treated as exclusive universal functions.

claim: The 2005 team study connected miRNA-guided cleavage of TAS precursor transcripts to the register of phased trans-acting siRNA production in Arabidopsis.

experimental_context.tissue: Arabidopsis tissues used for small-RNA analysis

limitations: Authorized use is bounded to verified title/abstract-level mechanism because no unrestricted full text was used here.
A cleavage signal does not by itself establish every downstream tasiRNA target or phenotype.

claim: In Arabidopsis TAS3a, AGO7-miR390 complexes used distinct cleavage and noncleavage modes at the two miR390 sites, showing that target-site roles cannot be inferred from complementarity alone.
limitations: The dual-site mechanism is established for the tested TAS3a system and should not be transferred to unrelated PHAS loci without matched evidence.
Abstract-only access limits unreported assay detail.

claim: A single miR173 target site could route tested non-TAS transcripts into phased siRNA production, and miR173 functioned with AGO1 during TAS1/TAS2 tasiRNA formation.

experimental_context.tissue: Arabidopsis transgenics and N. benthamiana transient leaves
experimental_context.genotype: wild type and small-RNA pathway mutants

limitations: Sufficiency is bounded to the tested constructs and cellular contexts.
It does not mean every miRNA-AGO1 complex triggers secondary siRNAs.

claim: During Turnip mosaic virus infection of Arabidopsis, most virus-derived siRNAs depended on DCL4 and RDR1, while full antiviral defense also required DCL2 and RDR6 in the tested mutant combinations.

entities.precursor: viral double-stranded or aberrant RNA substrates

experimental_context.treatment: wild-type or suppressor-deficient Turnip mosaic virus infection

limitations: Relative contributions are virus-, tissue-, allele- and infection-stage dependent.
vsiRNA abundance and resistance are distinct readouts and must not be collapsed.
A 2015 correction exists and requires downstream scope verification.

claim: Tested 22-nt Arabidopsis miRNAs had a distinctive capacity to trigger RDR6-dependent secondary siRNA production from target transcripts compared with many 21-nt miRNAs.
limitations: Length alone should not be treated as a universal trigger rule; duplex architecture, AGO loading, target context and assay design remain relevant.
The study does not convert predicted targets into verified secondary-siRNA pathways.

claim: Catalytic residues of AGO1, AGO2 and AGO7 were required to complement their respective Arabidopsis mutant defects; catalytically active AGO2 was required for local and systemic anti-Turnip mosaic virus activity in the tested assays.

experimental_context.genotype: ago mutants complemented with wild-type or slicer-defective AGO transgenes
experimental_context.treatment: Turnip mosaic virus infection and transient target assays

limitations: Catalysis requirements are bounded to tested alleles, targets and infection system.
AGO association or target coimmunoprecipitation alone does not establish target phenotype causality.

claim: Quantitative image phenotyping combined with molecular virus assays showed modular anti-Turnip crinkle virus roles for Arabidopsis AGOs: AGO2 and AGO7 were prominent and nonadditive in leaves, AGO3 had a smaller leaf role, and other AGOs contributed in inflorescences.

experimental_context.treatment: wild-type and viral-suppressor-deficient Turnip crinkle virus

limitations: AGO rankings are tissue- and virus-specific.
Image traits were paired with molecular assays; image color or growth alone would not establish antiviral mechanism.

claim: A 2025 multi-author study reported a correlation between POLD1 allelic differences and geminivirus resistance across diverse plants.
limitations: The verified title supports correlation, not a universal causal allele rule.
Carrington is a coauthor; the result is a team finding and not evidence of a personal framework.
Crop, virus and allele transfer require matched validation.

claim: In the tested cassava promoter-targeting system, controls supported CRISPR interference as sufficient for reduced nCBP expression, while the sufficiency and heritability of targeted DNA methylation remained unresolved.
limitations: The abstract explicitly leaves methylation sufficiency and heritability for future genetic segregation tests.
This work extends beyond small-RNA silencing and should be used as a timeline/crop-translation boundary, not as evidence for a miRNA mechanism.
Carrington is one coauthor among a broad team.

claim: The public record supports a career transition from Washington State plant-virus/PTGS work in the late 1990s, through Oregon State small-RNA pathway genetics and genomics in the 2000s, to Danforth leadership and an active crop-oriented research program from 2011 onward.
limitations: This is a public-career synthesis, not a claim about private motivations.
Institutional leadership does not establish authorship of every institutional scientific result.

claim: Current authoritative sources identify Carrington as a Danforth Member and Past President & CEO, with a continuing lab focused on RNA-mediated regulation, silencing, virus-host interactions and model-to-crop research.
limitations: Official profile supports current title and public research scope only.
It does not support specific mechanism claims, private opinions or sole ownership of team findings.

claim: Across the 1998, 2000, 2010 and 2019 research contexts, a recurring candidate framework is to separate the existence of antiviral silencing, the viral suppressor effect, the host pathway component, the tissue context and the disease phenotype rather than treating them as one validated mechanism.

experimental_context.tissue: transgene tissues, leaves, inflorescences and systemic tissues
experimental_context.genotype: study-specific suppressor, dcl, rdr and ago perturbations

limitations: This is an Agent synthesis of recurrent public team practice, not a named Carrington framework or personal quotation.
All supporting sources are Carrington-linked and do not constitute independent laboratory replication.

claim: A second candidate framework is combinatorial paralog decomposition: use single and higher-order mutants, matched molecular outputs and phenotype assays to distinguish specialization, redundancy and tissue dependence among DCL, RDR and AGO family members.

experimental_context.tissue: whole plants, leaves, inflorescences and systemic tissues as study-specific
experimental_context.treatment: virus infection or endogenous pathway analysis

limitations: This is an Agent-inferred research pattern, not a personal methodological statement.
Mutant combinations and phenotypes must be matched by virus, tissue, stage, allele and environment before transfer.

claim: A third candidate framework is trigger-context specificity: miRNA-guided cleavage can set a phase register, but entry into secondary-siRNA biogenesis depends on the tested miRNA-AGO pair, target-site architecture, transcript context and RDR6/DCL4 pathway evidence.

entities.target_gene: TAS1, TAS2, TAS3 and engineered targets

limitations: Agent synthesis; not a documented named framework.
Prediction or cleavage alone does not close secondary-siRNA function or phenotype.
The tested systems do not justify automatic transfer to reproductive phasiRNAs or unrelated crops.

claim: The public publication trajectory shows an evolution from plant-virus and RNA-silencing mechanism discovery, through Arabidopsis pathway genetics and small-RNA genomics, toward quantitative phenotyping and crop-oriented resistance/engineering collaborations.

entities.target_gene: POLD1, nCBP promoters and study-specific targets

experimental_context.treatment: virus infection, silencing perturbation or promoter targeting

limitations: This is a chronological Agent inference, not a claim of linear personal intent.
Recent crop papers are multi-team collaborations and extend beyond small-RNA mechanisms.
Publication sequence does not prove that older approaches were abandoned or superseded.

claim: Carrington's current official public scope joins RNA-mediated regulation of genes, genomes and viruses with genetics, genomics, computation, model systems and crop-relevant applications; the institutional page is an identity/scope source rather than mechanism evidence.
limitations: Institutional promotional text cannot establish a biochemical mechanism or the expert's private/current opinion on a disputed claim.
Current title is Member; Past President & CEO, not current President & CEO.

claim: In a public genomics interview, Carrington frames the virus problem as a sequence of questions about foreign recognition, host response and specific defense, then describes testing candidate host genes by mutant or transgenic perturbation followed by virus inoculation and susceptibility phenotyping.

experimental_context.genotype: mutant or transgenic candidate-gene lines versus parental wild type
experimental_context.assembly: Arabidopsis genome available at the time

limitations: The interview is historical and educational, not a current protocol or proof that every Carrington study follows the same sequence.
Susceptibility phenotypes alone do not identify the molecular step or exclude pleiotropy.

supporting_location.section: What is the big question?; candidate-gene follow-up

claim: Carrington publicly describes genome-scale measurements as discovery tools that can reveal unexpected regulated genes, followed by locus resolution, database-context review and focused experiments rather than treating differential expression as mechanism.
limitations: The interview discusses early microarrays, so modern sequencing-specific biases and multiplicity controls are not supplied.
Expression change is a candidate-generation observation, not direct target or causal evidence.

claim: The PNAS profile portrays Carrington's move from tobacco virology to Arabidopsis genetics as a model-system choice made to expose host-virus mechanisms, and it attributes the HC-Pro counterdefense hypothesis to convergence between viral genetics and parallel work rather than to a name-first narrative.

experimental_context.genotype: viral HC-Pro mutants and host models described historically

limitations: This is a journalist-written profile with attributed quotations, not a primary experimental account.
It cannot assign sole personal ownership to multi-laboratory discoveries.

supporting_location.section: Following His Hunches; RNA Silencing: A New Field

claim: A contemporaneous meeting report records Carrington distinguishing viral suppressors that converge on disrupted small-RNA function while acting differently: p19 and p21 associated with small-RNA duplexes, whereas HC-Pro did not in the reported assays.

experimental_context.tissue: transgenic Arabidopsis inflorescence summarized in the meeting report

limitations: The source is a third-party meeting report, not a verbatim transcript.
Underlying mechanistic claims must be cited to primary experiments before use as scientific facts.
Lack of detected HC-Pro association in those assays is not proof of no direct or cofactor-assisted RNA binding in all contexts.

claim: The 2014 University of Minnesota record verifies that Carrington publicly presented a lecture titled RNA Silencing Mechanisms in Plants, but it supplies no abstract, transcript, recording or Q&A from which scientific positions or response style can be reconstructed.
limitations: Inventory-only source: title and event context cannot support mechanism, quotation, analogy or Q&A reconstruction.

claim: Standing external work from the Baulcombe/Voinnet network found that diverse tested plant DNA and RNA viruses encoded suppressors of PTGS with distinct apparent modes of action, supporting viral counterdefense while arguing against one universal suppressor mechanism.
limitations: This is one author network and must not be counted as multiple independent laboratories when combined with its later papers.
PTGS reporter reversal supports suppression activity but does not by itself prove the same native infection target or symptom mechanism for every viral protein.

claim: The 1998 Brigneti et al. EMBO Journal article is retracted and must not be used as positive evidence for HC-Pro, 2b, PTGS suppression or antiviral RNAi, even though its broad topic has support from other standing studies.
limitations: A retraction invalidates this article as evidence; it is not automatically a demonstration that every individual biological proposition in the article is false.
Replacement support must come from standing primary studies and independently audited networks.

claim: The retraction of one early suppressor paper weakens that specific evidence edge but does not erase the broader counterdefense model, which retains standing support from independent PTGS, structural and RNA-binding studies; this is an evidence-network judgment, not a personal Carrington position.
limitations: The positive sources are mechanistically and taxonomically heterogeneous and cannot be merged into one universal suppressor mechanism.
Network independence is counted by laboratory network, not by paper count.

claim: Independent structural and biochemical work showed CIRV p19 binding a 21-nt siRNA duplex as a size-selective molecular caliper, directly supporting one sequestration mechanism but not a universal model for HC-Pro, 2b or all viral suppressors.
limitations: Only abstract-supported structural and binding conclusions are used here.
Binding a duplex does not by itself establish infection-stage necessity, host range or phenotype causality.

claim: An external multi-suppressor comparison found dsRNA binding across several unrelated viral suppressors but also separated size-selective small-duplex binding from size-independent long/short dsRNA binding, so convergent counterdefense does not imply identical molecular targets.

entities.precursor: long dsRNA and small dsRNA duplexes

experimental_context.tissue: plant and in vitro assay systems
experimental_context.treatment: viral suppressor expression and RNA binding

limitations: The authors proposed generality from a tested panel; untested suppressor families may act without dsRNA binding.
Binding specificity and in planta suppression necessity must be evaluated protein by protein.

claim: Independent Arabidopsis genetics and AGO-bound small-RNA data support AGO2 as an antiviral layer against TCV and CMV when AGO1-centered defense is compromised, while the lack of an AGO2 effect for TMV in that study limits any universal AGO2 claim.

experimental_context.tissue: Arabidopsis rosette and systemic infection tissues
experimental_context.genotype: ago mutant panel versus matched wild type

limitations: The Baulcombe network is counted once despite multiple related papers.
AGO effects depend on virus, suppressor target, tissue, infection time and AGO regulation; absence of phenotype in one assay is not universal absence.

supporting_location.page_or_figure: AGO mutant panel; AGO2 induction and bound vsiRNAs

claim: Independent Arabidopsis dcl genetics support DCL4 as the primary processor of endogenous RDR6-dependent tasiRNAs while revealing partial compensatory processing by DCL2 and DCL3 in specific mutant backgrounds.

experimental_context.tissue: whole seedlings/plants in the abstracted study

limitations: Only abstract-supported details are used.
Redundancy is substrate- and genotype-specific and does not mean DCL proteins are interchangeable in wild type or antiviral contexts.

claim: The Poethig laboratory independently resolved an Arabidopsis tasiRNA biogenesis pathway requiring RDR6/SGS3-associated conversion and DCL4 processing, supporting pathway decomposition beyond the Carrington laboratory while remaining an endogenous-developmental context rather than antiviral validation.

experimental_context.genotype: rdr6, sgs3 and dcl pathway mutants

limitations: Endogenous tasiRNA biogenesis does not automatically establish antiviral roles for the same factors.
Specific TAS loci, triggers and targets must remain distinct from viral siRNAs.

claim: Independent Nicotiana benthamiana knockdown experiments support an antiviral role for RDR6 across the tested virus panel, but the strength of the phenotype increased with growth temperature and included shoot-apex context, making host, temperature, tissue and suppressor status essential scope variables.

experimental_context.treatment: virus infection at compared growth temperatures

limitations: Knockdown is not a clean null and the tested Nicotiana/virus/temperature design does not establish universality across plants.
Broad-spectrum refers to the tested panel, not every virus or infection stage.

claim: Independent Arabidopsis immunoprecipitation and cleavage assays directly support AGO1 as a Slicer loaded with selected miRNAs, tasiRNAs and transgene siRNAs, while its failure to recover tested viral siRNAs and 24-nt chromatin siRNAs demonstrates loading specialization rather than a universal AGO1 cargo rule.

experimental_context.tissue: Arabidopsis inflorescence extracts and infected plants
experimental_context.treatment: immunoprecipitation, in vitro cleavage and virus infection

limitations: Cargo exclusion is limited to tested viruses, tissues, time points and assay sensitivity.
AGO1 loading and Slicer activity do not alone establish phenotype causality for any individual small-RNA target.

claim: Across independent networks, plant RNA silencing is best audited as a modular and conditional system: DCL processors can compensate in defined backgrounds, AGO antiviral contributions vary by virus and suppressor, and RDR6 effects depend on host, tissue and temperature; a single pathway label cannot substitute for component-level evidence.

experimental_context.treatment: virus infection or endogenous pathway analysis

limitations: This synthesis is an Agent inference, not an attributed personal Carrington rule.
The four experiments use different species, tissues, substrates and endpoints; they support a question framework, not one merged causal chain.

claim: A recurring Carrington-team reasoning pattern is to infer small-RNA pathway function from a multi-component genetic dependency map rather than from a single mutant or total small-RNA change.

experimental_context.tissue: whole seedlings or aerial tissue, study-dependent

limitations: Framework is reconstructed from team publications, not an explicit personal methods statement.
Most evidence is Arabidopsis-specific.

supporting_location.section: Results and abstracts across cited studies
supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: distinct DCL and RDR dependencies separate small-RNA classes.

claim: DCL4 is the principal processor for canonical Arabidopsis tasiRNAs, while other DCLs can produce alternative products when DCL4 is absent; residual products therefore require hierarchy tests rather than an independence claim.
limitations: The precise backup hierarchy is locus- and genotype-context dependent.
This does not imply that all 21-nt phasiRNAs in all plant species are DCL4 products.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: canonical tasiRNAs depend on DCL4, with alternative sizes in its absence.

claim: miRNA-guided target cleavage can establish the register for phased tasiRNA production, but the register must be demonstrated rather than inferred from a target prediction.
limitations: The Cell source was abstract-only in this run.
Cleavage/register evidence establishes biogenesis, not target or phenotype causality.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: cleavage positions align with phased small-RNA registers.

claim: Plant miRNA-guided cleavage is not by itself sufficient to commit a transcript to secondary-siRNA production; trigger length, AGO context, and/or target architecture provide additional determinants.

entities.mirna_family: miR173, miR390, miR828 and engineered guides

experimental_context.genotype: wild type, mutants, and engineered constructs

limitations: The two-hit mechanism is especially relevant to TAS3 and is not universal.
A 22-nt guide is a strong trigger feature in the tested systems, not an annotation criterion for miRNA identity.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: cleavage-competent interactions differ in secondary-siRNA output.

claim: In tested Arabidopsis and Nicotiana systems, converting an otherwise comparable guide from 21 nt to 22 nt can confer RDR6-dependent secondary-siRNA triggering competence.

entities.mirna_family: miR173, miR828, miR319 and engineered variants

experimental_context.genotype: wild type, pathway mutants, and transgenic/transient constructs

limitations: Construct sequence, precursor geometry, and AGO loading still require control.
The rule should not be generalized to every plant small RNA without testing.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: matched 22-nt guides trigger secondary siRNAs where 21-nt forms do not.

claim: The 5-prime nucleotide contributes to AGO sorting in Arabidopsis, but AGO7-miR390 specificity includes determinants beyond a simple first-base rule.
limitations: The AGO7 source was abstract-only in this run.
AGO sorting preferences vary across AGO proteins, tissues, and species.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: first-base identity influences sorting, while AGO7 retains specialized miR390 recognition.

claim: Catalytic-site AGO mutants, interpreted only after confirming protein accumulation and guide association, can separate loading/binding from slicer-dependent functions.

experimental_context.genotype: ago mutants complemented with wild-type or slicer-defective AGO

limitations: A single publication is direct method evidence but does not alone meet two-context framework recurrence.
Catalytic substitutions can have structural effects; matched expression/loading controls reduce but do not eliminate this concern.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: loaded slicer-defective AGO variants reveal catalysis-specific requirements.

claim: Genome-scale small-RNA profiles are most informative when stratified by pathway mutants and explicit locus/phase filters; profiling alone does not prove direct regulation.
limitations: Recurrent within one broad research program; independent laboratories strengthen scientific facts but not expert-style attribution.
Assembly and annotation versions constrain locus-level transfer.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: mutant-resolved profiles expose pathway dependencies and threshold-sensitive loci.

claim: Phased-locus discovery is threshold-sensitive; stringent and permissive criteria can yield different candidate sets, so negative discovery results must be bounded by the declared filter.
limitations: Single-study method inference.
Later algorithms and deeper sequencing may change candidate counts.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: relaxed filters recover candidates excluded by a stringent screen.

claim: Correlation between 24-nt siRNA loci, repeats, and heterochromatic marks does not establish that nearby protein-coding genes are directly regulated by those siRNAs.
limitations: The study provides limited evidence about nearby genes, not proof that no local direct regulation occurs.
Locus-specific tests are required.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: repeat-associated 24-nt loci rarely yielded evidence of direct nearby-gene control.

claim: TuMV P1/HC-Pro disrupts Arabidopsis miRNA-guided regulation and is associated with developmental abnormalities, but the evidence supports only a partial pathway-level explanation rather than one complete phenotype mechanism.

entities.target_gene: Scarecrow-like transcripts and other validated targets

experimental_context.genotype: wild type, infected plants, and suppressor transgenics

limitations: The foundational source was abstract-only in this run.
P1/HC-Pro is pleiotropic and is not a precise knockout of one host pathway.
Association between miRNA defects and morphology does not identify a single causal target.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: suppressor expression perturbs miRNA function, while single-target causality remains unsupported.

claim: Independent arf8 alleles do not support ARF8 misregulation as the key cause of P1/HC-Pro developmental defects, and a SALK T-DNA allele can confound rescue through transcriptional silencing of a 35S-driven transgene.

experimental_context.genotype: P1/HC-Pro transgenic plants crossed to arf8-6 and two independent arf8 mutations

limitations: This refutes a specific ARF8 model, not all miRNA-pathway contributions to suppressor phenotypes.
Transgene-silencing behavior is construct and locus dependent.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: independent arf8 mutations fail to reproduce the reported rescue.

claim: Small-RNA biogenesis, direct target regulation, and phenotype causality should be treated as separate evidentiary layers.

experimental_context.genotype: pathway mutants, viral suppressor transgenics, and independent target alleles

limitations: This is an inferred framework, not a direct quotation or personal statement.
The exact validation assay depends on the claim and system.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: pathway output, target action, and morphology require different tests.

claim: A strong phenotype-rescue design uses matched rescue constructs or multiple independent alleles and verifies the molecular intermediate, not morphology alone.

experimental_context.genotype: mutants plus wild-type/catalytic rescue or independent alleles

limitations: One source is Carrington-team work and one is independent critique; the preference is an inference from design choices.
Transgenic rescue remains sensitive to dosage and insertion position.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: mechanistic rescue requires matched molecular controls and independent genetics.

claim: Plant miRNAs, tasiRNAs/phasiRNAs, heterochromatic siRNAs, and viral siRNAs have distinguishable biogenesis dependencies and should not be merged into a generic small-RNA category for mechanistic inference.

entities.precursor: MIR hairpins, TAS transcripts, heterochromatic loci, and viral RNA

limitations: Pathway components can overlap or act redundantly, so distinctions are functional rather than absolute isolation.
Viral species and plant lineages can alter dependencies.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: distinct DCL/RDR combinations generate separable small-RNA populations.

claim: Well-controlled negative results should narrow a mechanistic model: failure to detect direct local regulation, failure to find candidates under declared filters, or failure of independent alleles to rescue all constrain scope.
limitations: Absence of evidence is bounded by assay sensitivity, sampling, and threshold.
This is a reconstructed reasoning pattern rather than explicit autobiographical guidance.

supporting_location.short_excerpt: Paraphrase: negative findings are retained as limits on causal scope.

claim: The 2015 correction to the independent 1999 PNAS viral-suppressor study reports duplicated rRNA loading panels and makes equal loading in Figure 1D unsupported; the record is corrected rather than retracted, so only claims independent of that loading inference may remain in standing evidence chains.

experimental_context.tissue: local and systemic plant tissue in the corrected study

limitations: The correction is publication-status evidence, not an independent replication or a new mechanistic experiment.
It does not retract the paper and does not by itself invalidate conclusions that do not rely on the affected equal-loading inference.
The corrected paper is external evidence and cannot establish a personal Carrington position.

claim: The 2015 correction to the 2010 TuMV Plant Cell study replaces an incorrect Figure 3A immunoblot panel and recalculates four coat-protein values while stating that the article conclusions are unaffected; exact Figure 3A or CP comparisons must therefore use the corrected presentation.

experimental_context.genotype: Col-0 and dcl mutant contexts from the corrected study

limitations: The correction is publication-status evidence and does not independently replicate the original antiviral experiments.
The notice preserves the article conclusions but does not authorize reuse of the uncorrected Figure 3A panel or CP values.
The corrected qualitative result remains bounded to the tested Arabidopsis genotypes, TuMV constructs, tissues and time points.
